issue.title: test_sidecar_clone_retries_transient_transport_failures fails: monkeypatch target sase.sdd._store_link.time.sleep does not exist
issue.description:
`just check-full` (run during sase-th.7, the land phase of epic sase-th "Repair the red
master CI lanes") fails exactly one test out of 36846:

tests/sdd_store/test_sidecar_clone.py::test_sidecar_clone_retries_transient_transport_failures

The test does `monkeypatch.setattr("sase.sdd._store_link.time.sleep", sleeps.append)`, but
`src/sase/sdd/_store_link.py` never does `import time` — it has no `time` attribute to patch.
The retry-with-sleep logic this test exercises actually lives in `clone_sdd_store()` at
src/sase/sdd/_store_clone_ops.py:126 (`time.sleep(delay)`), which `_store_link.py` calls
through `from sase.sdd._store_clone_ops import clone_sdd_store`.

This test was added by commit 770777110 ("fix(sdd): harden remote sidecar cloning"), which
landed on master this morning (2026-08-25 07:19 EDT). It is unrelated to epic sase-th: none of
that epic's six phases (symvision cleanup, bead-notes fixtures, marker-path audit, PNG
goldens, pooled-alias cursor, CI-only test races) touch the sdd store.

Fix: repoint the monkeypatch target to `sase.sdd._store_clone_ops.time.sleep`.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic ImportError, not intermittent: monkeypatch.setattr resolves the dotted path sase.sdd._store_link.time and fails because _store_link.py never imports the time module. Reproduces on every run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/sdd_store/test_sidecar_clone.py::test_sidecar_clone_retries_transient_transport_failures -v fails with ImportError: import error in sase.sdd._store_link.time: No module named 'sase.sdd._store_link.time'; 'sase.sdd._store_link' is not a package.
